name: Biology
topics: Living things: characteristics and organisation of life
The cell: structure and cell processes
Ecology: ecosystems, food chains and energy flow

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic common to all living things?
questions.e: All living things respire, excrete waste and grow, but not all of them move their whole body from one place to another. For example, plants are rooted to the soil and do not show locomotion, yet they are still alive.
questions.p: All living things dey breathe, dey waste out and dey grow, but no be all of dem dey waka comot one place go another place. Plant dey stay for ground, e no dey waka, but e still dey alive well well.

questions.q: Arrange the following levels of biological organisation in order from the simplest to the most complex: (i) Organ (ii) Cell (iii) Tissue (iv) Organ system
questions.e: The correct order of organisation, from simplest to most complex, is cell, tissue, organ, then organ system. Cells group to form tissues, tissues group to form organs, and organs group to form organ systems.
questions.p: The correct order na cell, then tissue, then organ, then organ system. Cells join together make tissue, tissue join make organ, organ join make organ system.

questions.q: A toddler in a market in Enugu accidentally touched a hot stove and immediately pulled her hand away. This quick reaction to a stimulus is an example of which characteristic of living things?
questions.e: Irritability, also called sensitivity, is the ability of a living thing to detect a stimulus (like heat) and respond to it. The toddler sensed the heat from the stove and quickly withdrew her hand, showing this characteristic.
questions.p: Irritability (or sensitivity) na when living thing sense something (like heat) and respond quick quick. The small pikin sense the hot stove and comot im hand fast, na so irritability dey show.

questions.q: A single-celled amoeba increases in size over several hours, after which its nucleus divides and the cell splits into two identical daughter cells. This observation best illustrates a combination of which two characteristics of living things?
questions.e: The increase in size of the amoeba shows growth, while the splitting into two identical daughter cells shows reproduction (asexual, by binary fission). Both characteristics occur together in this process.
questions.p: The amoeba wey dey enlarge na growth, and the one wey split to two identical cells na reproduction (binary fission). So the two characteristics, growth and reproduction, dey happen together for this process.

questions.q: In the human body, many red blood cells group together and work with blood plasma to transport oxygen and nutrients round the body. This grouping of similar cells performing a common function is best described as a
questions.e: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform a common function. Red blood cells and plasma working together to transport substances form blood, which is a tissue.
questions.p: Tissue na when similar cells come together to do one common work. Red blood cells and plasma wey dey carry oxygen and food go body na blood, and blood na tissue.

questions.q: A potted maize seedling placed close to a classroom window was observed, after some days, to bend and grow towards the direction of the incoming sunlight. Which characteristic of living things is primarily demonstrated by this behaviour?
questions.e: The seedling bending towards light is a response to a stimulus (light), which is called irritability or sensitivity. Although growth movements are involved, the key characteristic being shown is the plant's ability to detect and respond to the light stimulus.
questions.p: The seedling wey bend go where light dey show say e dey respond to stimulus (light), and dat one na irritability or sensitivity. Although growth dey involved small, the main characteristic wey dey show na how the plant fit sense and respond to the light.

questions.q: Which cell organelle controls the activities of the cell and contains the hereditary material (DNA)?
questions.e: The nucleus contains the chromosomes (DNA) and directs all the activities of the cell. Mitochondria release energy, ribosomes make proteins, and the Golgi apparatus packages substances.
questions.p: Nucleus na im get the DNA wey dey control everything wey dey happen for the cell. Mitochondria na for energy, ribosome na for protein, Golgi apparatus na for packaging.

questions.q: The net movement of molecules or ions from a region of their higher concentration to a region of their lower concentration until the particles are evenly spread is best described as:
questions.e: This movement of molecules/ions from high to low concentration without using energy is diffusion. Osmosis is specifically for water across a membrane, and active transport needs energy to move substances against their concentration gradient.
questions.p: Na diffusion be dis one, because e be movement of molecules from where dem plenty to where dem small, no energy dey use. Osmosis na for water only, active transport need energy.

questions.q: Ngozi placed some red blood cells into a beaker of distilled water. After some minutes, the cells swelled up and burst. Which term describes this process and why did it happen?
o: Turgidity; water entered the cells by active transport
Haemolysis; water entered the cells by osmosis
Crenation; water left the cells by osmosis
Plasmolysis; water left the cells by diffusion
questions.e: Distilled water has a higher water concentration than the cell cytoplasm, so water moves into the red blood cells by osmosis, making them swell and burst; this is called haemolysis. Crenation is shrinking, and plasmolysis applies to plant cells with cell walls.
questions.p: Distilled water get plenty water pass wetin dey inside the blood cell, so water enter the cell by osmosis make e swell burst — dem dey call am haemolysis. Crenation na when cell shrink, plasmolysis na for plant cell wey get cell wall.

questions.q: A piece of Irish potato tissue is placed in a concentrated salt solution for 30 minutes. Which of the following correctly describes what would be observed and the reason?
o: The tissue becomes flaccid because water moves out of the cells by osmosis
The tissue remains unchanged because the cell membrane is impermeable to water
The tissue increases in mass because salt moves into the cells by diffusion
The tissue becomes turgid because water moves into the cells by osmosis
questions.e: The concentrated salt solution has less water (lower water potential) than the potato cell sap, so water moves out of the cells by osmosis, causing the tissue to lose turgor and become flaccid (soft). This is the opposite of what happens in distilled water.
questions.p: The strong salt solution no get plenty water pass wetin dey inside potato cell, so water comot from the cell go outside by osmosis, make the potato soft (flaccid). Na opposite of wetin go happen for distilled water.

questions.q: Two sugar solutions, P and Q, are separated by a selectively permeable membrane in a visking tubing set-up. Solution P has a higher sugar concentration than solution Q. In which direction will water move, and what will happen to solution P?
o: Water moves from P to Q; solution P decreases in volume
Water moves from Q to P; solution P increases in volume
Water moves from P to Q; solution P increases in volume
No net movement of water occurs because both are sugar solutions
questions.e: Water always moves by osmosis from a region of lower solute concentration (higher water potential), which is Q, to a region of higher solute concentration (lower water potential), which is P. As water enters P, its volume increases.
questions.p: Water dey waka by osmosis comot from where water plenty (Q) go where water small (P, because sugar plenty there). As water enter P, P go increase for volume.

questions.q: In an experiment, equal-sized potato chips were soaked in four sugar solutions for one hour: 1 mol/dm3, 0.5 mol/dm3, 0.25 mol/dm3, and distilled water. The chip in distilled water gained the most mass, while the chip in 1 mol/dm3 solution lost the most mass. What can be correctly concluded from this result?
o: Distilled water has a higher solute concentration than the potato cell sap
The potato cells are impermeable to water molecules
The cell sap of the potato has a lower solute concentration than the 1 mol/dm3 solution
The cell sap of the potato has a higher solute concentration than the 1 mol/dm3 solution
questions.e: Since the chip lost water (mass) in the 1 mol/dm3 solution, water must have left the potato cells, meaning the solution had a higher solute concentration (lower water potential) than the cell sap. This shows the potato cell sap's solute concentration is lower than 1 mol/dm3.
questions.p: Since the potato lose water for the 1 mol/dm3 solution, e mean say water comot from the potato cell go outside, so the solution get more solute pass the potato cell sap. Dis mean the potato cell sap no reach 1 mol/dm3 for solute concentration.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the main purpose of mitosis in a growing yam plant?
o: To reduce the chromosome number by half
To introduce genetic variation among offspring
To produce two genetically identical daughter cells for growth and repair
questions.e: Mitosis is the type of cell division that produces two daughter cells identical to the parent cell. It is responsible for growth, repair of worn-out tissues, and asexual reproduction, not for making gametes or creating variation.
questions.p: Mitosis na the cell division wey dey produce two daughter cells wey be exact copy of the parent cell. E dey help plant grow and repair damaged tissue, e no be for making gametes or variation.

questions.q: During which stage of mitosis do the chromosomes line up at the equator (middle) of the cell before they separate?
questions.e: In metaphase, the chromosomes arrange themselves at the equatorial plate of the cell, attached to spindle fibres, ready to be pulled apart in anaphase.
questions.p: For metaphase, the chromosomes go line up for the middle (equator) of the cell, dem don attach to spindle fibre, waiting make dem separate for anaphase.

questions.q: A body cell of a cassava plant contains 36 chromosomes. How many chromosomes will each gamete produced through meiosis in this plant contain?
questions.e: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half to produce gametes with the haploid number. Since the body (diploid) cell has 36 chromosomes, each gamete will have 36/2 = 18 chromosomes.
questions.p: Meiosis dey reduce chromosome number by half make gametes get haploid number. Since the body cell get 36 chromosomes, each gamete go get 36/2 = 18 chromosomes.

questions.q: Which of these is a key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
o: Mitosis involves crossing over while meiosis does not
Mitosis maintains the chromosome number while meiosis reduces it by half
Mitosis produces four daughter cells while meiosis produces two
Mitosis occurs only in animals while meiosis occurs only in plants
questions.e: Mitosis produces two daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent cell (diploid to diploid), while meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half to produce haploid gametes. Crossing over occurs in meiosis, not mitosis, and both processes occur in plants and animals.
questions.p: Mitosis dey produce two daughter cells wey get the same chromosome number as the parent (diploid to diploid), but meiosis dey reduce the number by half make e produce haploid gametes. Crossing over dey happen for meiosis, no be mitosis.

questions.q: A student observed that offspring from the same pair of groundnut plants show different seed sizes and colours. Which event during meiosis mainly causes this kind of variation?
o: Equal division of cytoplasm during telophase
Replication of DNA before meiosis begins
Crossing over and independent assortment of chromosomes
Formation of a single spindle fibre in each cell
questions.e: Crossing over exchanges genetic material between homologous chromosomes, and independent assortment shuffles chromosomes randomly into gametes. These two events together create new combinations of genes, leading to variation among offspring of the same parents.
questions.p: Crossing over dey exchange gene material between homologous chromosomes, and independent assortment dey mix up chromosomes anyhow enter gametes. Dis two tins together dey create new combination of genes wey cause variation among offspring from the same parents.

questions.q: An organism has a diploid chromosome number of 24. After meiosis I is completed, what will be the chromosome number in each resulting cell, and how many chromatids will each chromosome have at that point?
questions.e: In meiosis I, homologous chromosomes separate, halving the chromosome number from 24 to 12. However, sister chromatids only separate in meiosis II, so at the end of meiosis I each chromosome still has 2 chromatids.
questions.p: For meiosis I, homologous chromosomes dey separate, so the number go reduce from 24 to 12. But sister chromatids go only separate for meiosis II, so after meiosis I, each chromosome still get 2 chromatids.

questions.q: Which arrangement correctly shows the taxonomic hierarchy from the largest (most inclusive) group to the smallest (least inclusive) group?
o: Phylum, Kingdom, Order, Class, Genus, Family, Species
Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom
Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.e: The standard taxonomic hierarchy, from broadest to most specific, is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. This order groups organisms from very general categories down to very specific ones.
questions.p: Di correct order from di biggest group to di smallest na Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. Dis one dey arrange tins from general to specific.

questions.q: Which of the following is the smallest and most basic unit used in the classification of living things?
questions.e: Species is the smallest unit of classification and consists of organisms that can interbreed freely to produce fertile offspring. Genus, Family, and Class are larger groups that contain many species.
questions.p: Species na di smallest unit wey dem dey use classify living tins, e be organisms wey fit mate well-well produce pikin wey fit still born pikin. Genus, Family, and Class don already big pass species.

questions.q: A student wants to write the scientific name of the Nile tilapia fish correctly, given that its genus is 'Oreochromis' and its species name is 'niloticus'. Which of the options below follows the correct rule of binomial nomenclature?
questions.e: In binomial nomenclature, the genus name is written first with a capital letter, followed by the species name in small letters. So 'Oreochromis niloticus' is correct, while the other options break this rule.
questions.p: For binomial nomenclature, di genus name go come first wit capital letter, den di species name go follow wit small letter. So 'Oreochromis niloticus' na di correct way, di oda ones no follow di rule.

questions.q: Two newly discovered insects, Ayo's beetle and Bimbo's beetle, are found to belong to the same Order but different Families. Based on the rules of the taxonomic hierarchy, which of the following must also be true about these two insects?
o: They must belong to the same Class
They must belong to the same Family
They must belong to the same Species
They must belong to the same Genus
questions.e: In the taxonomic hierarchy, Order is nested inside Class, so organisms sharing the same Order must also share the same Class, Phylum and Kingdom. However, being in the same Order does not force them to share the same Family, Genus or Species, since those are smaller, more specific groups.
questions.p: For taxonomic hierarchy, Order dey inside Class, so if two organisms dey same Order, dem go still dey same Class, Phylum and Kingdom. But e no mean say dem go dey same Family, Genus or Species, becos dat one dey more specific pass Order.

questions.q: Which of the following is the green pigment found in chloroplasts that traps light energy for photosynthesis?
questions.e: Chlorophyll is the green pigment found in chloroplasts that absorbs light energy (mainly red and blue light) for photosynthesis. Carotene, xanthophyll and anthocyanin are other plant pigments but they do not directly trap light for photosynthesis.
questions.p: Chlorophyll na di green pigment wey dey inside chloroplast wey dey catch light energy for photosynthesis. Carotene, xanthophyll and anthocyanin na other pigments but dem no dey directly use light make photosynthesis happen.

questions.q: Which pair of substances are the raw materials used by green plants during photosynthesis?
questions.e: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide (from the air) and water (from the soil) as raw materials, together with light energy and chlorophyll, to produce glucose and oxygen. Oxygen and glucose are products, not raw materials.
questions.p: Photosynthesis dey use carbon dioxide (from air) and water (from soil) as di raw materials, plus light and chlorophyll, to produce glucose and oxygen. Oxygen and glucose na products, dem no be raw materials.

questions.q: In which part of the chloroplast does the light-dependent stage of photosynthesis mainly take place?
questions.e: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis occur on the thylakoid membranes, which are stacked together to form the grana inside the chloroplast. The stroma, by contrast, is where the light-independent (dark) reactions take place.
questions.p: Di light stage of photosynthesis dey happen for thylakoid membrane wey dem stack together to form grana inside chloroplast. Na stroma na where di dark stage (light-independent) dey happen.

questions.q: A student destarched a potted plant by keeping it in the dark for 48 hours. One leaf was then covered on both sides with black paper, leaving the rest of the leaf exposed, and the plant was placed in sunlight for several hours. The covered leaf was later removed, boiled in water, decolourised in alcohol, and tested with iodine solution. What result should the student expect?
o: The covered part remains brown-orange while the uncovered part turns blue-black
The whole leaf turns blue-black with iodine
The whole leaf remains brown-orange after testing
The covered part turns blue-black while the uncovered part remains brown-orange
questions.e: Covering part of the leaf with black paper stops light from reaching that part, so no photosynthesis occurs there and no starch is made; iodine will not turn that part blue-black, it stays brown-orange. The uncovered part receives light, makes starch, and turns blue-black with iodine.
questions.p: If you cover part of di leaf with black paper, light no go reach dat part, so photosynthesis no go happen and no starch go form; iodine no go turn dat part blue-black, e go remain brown-orange. Di part wey light reach go get starch and turn blue-black when you put iodine.

questions.q: In an experiment with aquatic plants in a pond, it was observed that at low light intensity, the rate of photosynthesis increased steadily as light intensity increased. However, beyond a certain light intensity, further increases in light no longer raised the rate of photosynthesis, even though carbon dioxide and water were still available. This observation best illustrates which concept?
questions.e: At low light intensity, light is the limiting factor, so increasing it raises the rate of photosynthesis. Beyond a certain point, another factor (such as carbon dioxide concentration or temperature) becomes limiting instead, so the rate levels off even though light keeps increasing. This is the law of limiting factors.
questions.p: For low light, light na di limiting factor, so as e dey increase, photosynthesis rate dey increase. But after certain point, another factor (like carbon dioxide or temperature) go become di limiting one, so di rate go level off even as light still dey increase. Na so dem dey call di law of limiting factors.

questions.q: An organism that feeds by taking in complex, ready-made organic food (such as plant or animal matter), digesting it internally, and then absorbing the useful products is said to show which type of nutrition?
questions.e: Holozoic nutrition is seen in most animals, including man; it involves taking in solid food, digesting it inside the body, and absorbing the digested products. Autotrophic organisms make their own food, while saprophytes feed on dead or decaying matter externally.
questions.p: Holozoic nutrition na when animal chop solid food wey already ready, digest am inside body, then absorb the useful part. Autotroph dey make dia own food, saprophyte dey chop dead or rotten things.

questions.q: Mama Ngozi chewed a piece of boiled yam for some time before swallowing it, and she noticed it began to taste slightly sweet. Which enzyme present in her saliva is responsible for this change?
questions.e: Ptyalin, also called salivary amylase, breaks down starch in the yam into simpler sugars like maltose, which taste sweet. Pepsin and trypsin act on proteins, while lipase acts on fats, so they are not responsible for this effect.
questions.p: Ptyalin (salivary amylase) dey break down the starch wey dey the yam to sugar, na why e begin taste sweet small small. Pepsin and trypsin na for protein, lipase na for fat, so dem no fit cause the sweet taste.

questions.q: A hunter examining the skull of a bush dog noticed long, pointed, curved teeth located just behind the front teeth on each side of the jaw. What is the main function of these teeth?
questions.e: The long, pointed, curved teeth described are canines, which are well developed in carnivores like dogs for tearing and piercing flesh during feeding. Grinding and crushing are functions of molars and premolars, while cutting is mainly done by incisors.
questions.p: The long pointed teeth wey curve na canine, dem dey help the dog tear and pierce meat. Molar and premolar na for grind and crush, incisor na for cut food small small.

questions.q: The inner wall of the small intestine has many tiny, finger-like projections. What is the main importance of these structures in digestion?
o: They neutralize excess bile from the liver
They increase the surface area for absorption of digested food
They produce hydrochloric acid for digestion
questions.e: These finger-like projections are called villi, and their main role is to increase the surface area of the small intestine so that digested food substances like glucose and amino acids can be absorbed quickly into the blood. Acid production and bile neutralisation occur elsewhere in the digestive system.
questions.p: Dis small finger-like things na villi, dem dey increase the surface area so body fit absorb digested food like glucose and amino acid quick quick. Acid and bile matter dey happen for other part of the gut.

questions.q: A goat has a dental formula of 0.0.3.3 / 3.1.3.3, meaning the upper jaw has no incisors or canines but has 3 premolars and 3 molars on each side, while the lower jaw has 3 incisors, 1 canine, 3 premolars and 3 molars on each side. What is the total number of teeth in the goat's complete set?
questions.e: Add the teeth on one side of the upper jaw: 0+0+3+3 = 6, and one side of the lower jaw: 3+1+3+3 = 10, giving 16 teeth on one side (upper and lower combined). Since teeth occur on both the left and right sides of the jaw, multiply by 2: 16 x 2 = 32 teeth in total.
questions.p: If you add the teeth for one side of up jaw: 0+0+3+3 = 6, and one side of down jaw: 3+1+3+3 = 10, e go give 16 teeth for one side. Since teeth dey both left and right side, multiply the 16 by 2 to get 32 teeth total.

questions.q: Which tissue is mainly responsible for transporting water and dissolved mineral salts from the root to the leaves in a flowering plant such as maize?
questions.e: Xylem vessels are dead, hollow tubes that carry water and mineral salts upward from the root to other parts of the plant. Phloem instead transports manufactured food like sugars. The cambium and cortex are not transport tissues.
questions.p: Xylem na the tube wey dey carry water and mineral salt from root go leaf. Phloem na for food transport, e no be water. Cambium and cortex no be transport tissue at all.

questions.q: In human beings, which blood component is mainly responsible for carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body tissues?
questions.e: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it in the tissues. Plasma carries dissolved substances but not oxygen in large amounts. Platelets help in clotting, while white blood cells fight infection.
questions.p: Red blood cells get haemoglobin wey dey hold oxygen from lungs go the body tissues. Plasma na liquid wey carry other substances, e no be oxygen carrier. Platelets na for clotting, white blood cells na for fight sickness.

questions.q: A student places a potted plant in the school garden under bright sun with a gentle breeze blowing. Which combination of conditions below would most likely increase the rate of transpiration in this plant?
o: Low light intensity and still air
questions.e: High temperature increases the kinetic energy of water molecules, making them evaporate faster from the leaf surface, while strong wind blows away the water vapour quickly, keeping the air around the leaf dry and increasing the rate of water loss. The other options describe cool, humid or still conditions which slow down transpiration.
questions.p: When temperature high, water for leaf go evaporate faster, and when wind strong, e go carry the water vapour commot quick quick, so transpiration go dey fast. The other options na cool or wet condition wey go slow transpiration down.

questions.q: In the human circulatory system, which chamber of the heart receives oxygenated blood coming directly from the lungs?
questions.e: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium. The right atrium and right ventricle deal with deoxygenated blood from the body, while the left ventricle receives blood from the left atrium before pumping it to the body.
questions.p: Pulmonary vein dey carry oxygen-rich blood from lungs enter left atrium. Right atrium and right ventricle dey handle blood wey never get oxygen, while left ventricle na im dey collect from left atrium before e pump am comot go body.

questions.q: A student cut a leafy twig and placed the cut end in a beaker of water containing red eosin dye, then kept the setup in bright sunlight. After two hours, the dye had risen noticeably up the stem into the leaf veins. Which of the following best explains the main force responsible for this upward movement, given that the twig has no roots?
o: Capillary action alone within the xylem vessels
Root pressure generated by osmotic absorption of water
Transpiration pull created by water loss from the leaf surface
Active transport by companion cells pushing the dye upward
questions.e: Since the twig has been cut and has no roots, root pressure cannot be responsible for the movement. As water evaporates from the leaf surface (transpiration), it creates a pulling force (tension) that draws water and the dissolved dye upward through the continuous xylem column, a process called transpiration pull.
questions.p: Because dem don cut the twig and e no get root again, root pressure no fit be the reason. Na transpiration (water wey dey comot from leaf) dey create pulling force wey dey drag water and the dye go up inside the xylem, dem dey call am transpiration pull.

questions.q: Fish rely on a single circulatory system in which blood passes through the heart once for every complete circuit of the body, while mammals use a double circulatory system in which blood passes through the heart twice. What is the main advantage of the double circulatory system over the single one in terms of efficient transport of oxygen to body tissues?
o: It allows blood to bypass the lungs completely whenever the animal is resting
It allows blood to be re-pressurised at the heart after passing through the lungs, maintaining higher blood pressure for efficient delivery to body tissues
It removes the need for a muscular heart in large, active animals
It reduces the total number of blood vessels needed in the body
questions.e: In single circulation, blood loses pressure as it passes through the lung capillaries before reaching the body, making delivery slower. In double circulation, blood returns to the heart after the lungs and is pumped again at higher pressure to the body, allowing faster and more efficient oxygen supply to tissues, which suits active animals like mammals.
questions.p: For single circulation, blood go lose pressure as e pass through lung capillaries before e reach body, so delivery go slow. For double circulation, blood go first return go heart after lungs, dem go pump am again with more pressure go body, so oxygen go reach tissue fast well well, dis one good pass for active animals like mammal.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines respiration in living organisms?
o: The breakdown of food substances to release energy for life processes
The intake of food substances into the body for use
The removal of metabolic waste products from the body
The building up of complex molecules from simple ones
questions.e: Respiration is the process by which cells break down food (like glucose) to release energy needed for life activities such as growth and movement. It is not the same as feeding, excretion or building up of molecules.
questions.p: Respiration na how cell dey break down food to release energy wey body need to work and move. E no be the same thing as eating, waste removal or building up molecule.

questions.q: In which cell organelle does aerobic respiration mainly take place?
questions.e: The mitochondrion is often called the 'powerhouse of the cell' because it is where most aerobic respiration occurs and ATP (energy) is produced. The nucleus controls cell activities, ribosomes make proteins, and the Golgi apparatus packages substances.
questions.p: Mitochondrion na the 'power house' of cell, na there most aerobic respiration dey happen make energy (ATP) come out. Nucleus dey control cell, ribosome dey make protein, Golgi apparatus dey package things.

questions.q: Which of the following word equations correctly represents aerobic respiration?
o: Carbon dioxide + Water -> Glucose + Oxygen (energy absorbed)
Glucose + Oxygen -> Carbon dioxide + Water (energy released)
questions.e: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen to fully break down glucose into carbon dioxide and water, releasing a large amount of energy. The first option describes photosynthesis, while the other two describe anaerobic respiration in yeast and in muscles respectively.
questions.p: Aerobic respiration dey use oxygen to break glucose finish into carbon dioxide and water, e dey release plenty energy. First option na photosynthesis, the other two na anaerobic respiration for yeast and for muscle.

questions.q: During the local brewing of burukutu (a traditional Nigerian alcoholic drink) from guinea corn, yeast cells respire anaerobically on the sugars present. Which pair of substances is produced as the main end-products of this process?
questions.e: When yeast respires without oxygen (anaerobic respiration), it breaks down sugar into ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide, a process called fermentation. This is the basis for brewing drinks like burukutu and palm wine.
questions.p: When yeast dey respire without oxygen (anaerobic respiration), e dey break sugar turn ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide, dem dey call am fermentation. Na this process dem dey use brew burukutu and palm wine.

questions.q: In an experiment, a locust was placed in a respirometer. During one hour, it consumed 60 cm^3 of oxygen and produced 48 cm^3 of carbon dioxide. Calculate the respiratory quotient (RQ) of the locust.
questions.e: Respiratory Quotient (RQ) = volume of CO2 produced / volume of O2 consumed = 48/60 = 0.8. This value is typical for respiration involving a mixture of carbohydrates and fats.
questions.p: Respiratory Quotient (RQ) = volume of CO2 wey come out divide by volume of O2 wey enter = 48/60 = 0.8. This number dey normal when body dey use carbohydrate and fat mix for respiration.

questions.q: Chidi sprinted 100 metres during an inter-house sports competition in his school. After the race, he continued to breathe heavily and rapidly for some minutes even though he had stopped running. Which of the following best explains this observation?
o: His muscles had respired anaerobically, producing lactic acid that created an oxygen debt which must be repaid
His muscles switched completely to aerobic respiration during the sprint
His lungs were filled with excess carbon dioxide from photosynthesis
His body temperature dropped suddenly, increasing his breathing rate
questions.e: During intense exercise, oxygen supply to muscles cannot keep up with demand, so muscles respire anaerobically and build up lactic acid, creating an 'oxygen debt'. After the race, fast heavy breathing supplies extra oxygen to break down the lactic acid and repay this debt.
questions.p: When person dey run fast-fast, the oxygen wey enter body no dey reach muscle sharp-sharp, so muscle go respire anaerobically make lactic acid build up, dem dey call am 'oxygen debt'. After race, the fast breathing na to bring extra oxygen come clear the lactic acid and pay back the debt.

questions.q: Excretion in living organisms is best defined as the:
o: breakdown of large food molecules into simpler ones
removal of undigested food materials from the body
removal of metabolic waste products from the body
movement of digested food from the gut into the blood
questions.e: Excretion is the removal of waste products made inside the body as a result of metabolism, such as carbon(IV) oxide, urea and excess water. Undigested food is not a metabolic waste, so its removal is called egestion.
questions.p: Excretion na when body remove waste wey come from inside metabolism, like CO2, urea and plenty water. Undigested food no be metabolism waste, so to remove am na egestion.

questions.q: Which organ is mainly responsible for removing carbon(IV) oxide and water vapour from the body as excretory products?
questions.e: The lungs remove carbon(IV) oxide and some water vapour produced during respiration when we breathe out. The kidney removes urea and excess water mainly as urine, while the liver and skin have other excretory roles.
questions.p: Na lungs dey remove CO2 and some water vapour wey respiration produce, when we dey breathe out. Kidney dey remove urea and extra water as urine, liver and skin get their own small work too.

questions.q: In the human kidney, blood is first filtered to begin the formation of urine at the:
questions.e: The glomerulus is a knot of capillaries inside the Bowman's capsule where high blood pressure forces water, salts, urea and glucose out of the blood into the capsule; this process is called ultrafiltration. The other structures act later in reabsorption or transport of urine.
questions.p: Glomerulus na the small blood vessels wey dey inside Bowman's capsule, na there high pressure dey push water, salt, urea and glucose comot from blood enter the capsule, dem call am ultrafiltration. Other parts dey work later for reabsorption or to carry urine comot.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why egestion is not regarded as a form of excretion?
o: Egested materials are formed only during respiration
Egested materials never entered the body cells or blood
Egestion takes place only in green plants
Egested materials are always in liquid form
questions.e: Egestion is the removal of undigested food as faeces, and this food never actually entered the blood or body cells to take part in metabolism. Excretion, on the other hand, removes waste that was produced by chemical reactions inside the cells.
questions.p: Egestion na to remove the food wey no digest as faeces, and that food never enter blood or body cells at all. Excretion na to remove waste wey come from inside the cells after chemical reactions.

questions.q: The skin assists the body in excretion mainly through the activity of the:
questions.e: Sweat glands in the skin produce sweat, which contains water, salts and small amounts of urea, and this is released onto the skin surface as an excretory product. Sebaceous glands produce oil for the skin and are not involved in excretion.
questions.p: Na sweat glands for skin dey make sweat, wey get water, salt and small urea inside, and dem dey release am come skin surface as waste. Sebaceous glands na for oil, dem no dey do excretion work.

questions.q: A student noticed that when a person is dehydrated after a long trek under the hot Sokoto sun, the kidneys produce a small volume of highly concentrated urine. Which explanation correctly accounts for this observation?
o: Reduced blood flow completely stops filtration at the glomerulus
Increased ADH secretion raises water reabsorption in the collecting duct
Decreased ADH secretion raises water reabsorption in the collecting duct
Increased aldosterone secretion reduces sodium reabsorption in the nephron
questions.e: When the body is short of water, the blood becomes more concentrated and this is detected by the brain, which signals the pituitary gland to release more antidiuretic hormone (ADH). More ADH makes the collecting duct walls more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed back into the blood, leaving a small amount of concentrated urine.
questions.p: When body no get enough water, blood dey more concentrated and brain go sense am, e go tell pituitary gland make e release more ADH. The ADH go make collecting duct allow more water pass back inside blood, so wetin remain na small concentrated urine.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the skeletal system in man?
questions.e: The skeleton supports the body, protects organs and gives attachment to muscles. Digestive enzymes are produced by glands such as the salivary glands, stomach and pancreas, not by bones.
questions.p: Bone dey support body, protect organs and give muscle attachment. But e no be bone dey produce digestive enzymes, na glands like salivary gland, stomach and pancreas dey do am.

questions.q: The human skeleton is divided into two main parts: the axial skeleton and the ___ skeleton.
questions.e: The axial skeleton includes the skull, vertebral column and rib cage, while the appendicular skeleton includes the limbs, shoulder girdle and pelvic girdle. Together they make up the whole human skeleton.
questions.p: Axial skeleton na skull, backbone and ribcage. Appendicular skeleton na the hand, leg, shoulder and pelvic bones. The two together be the full human skeleton.

questions.q: Which type of joint is found between the flat bones of an adult human skull?
questions.e: The bones of the skull are joined by sutures, which are fixed, fibrous joints that do not allow movement. This protects the brain by keeping the skull rigid.
questions.p: The skull bones dey join by sutures, wey be fibrous joint wey no dey move. Dis one dey help protect the brain because e dey make the skull strong and firm.

questions.q: The knee joint allows the lower leg to move forward and backward in one plane only, like the movement of a door on its hinges. This type of joint is called a
questions.e: A hinge joint, like the knee and elbow, allows movement in only one plane, similar to how a door swings on its hinge. This is different from a ball and socket joint which allows movement in many directions.
questions.p: Hinge joint, like knee and elbow, dey allow movement for only one direction, just like how door dey swing for im hinge. Dis one different from ball and socket joint wey fit move for plenty direction.

questions.q: Chidinma, an SS3 student, noticed she could turn her head from side to side as if saying "no", but she could not twist her knee in the same way. Which joint allows this side-to-side rotation of the head?
o: Hinge joint between the skull and vertebral column
Ball and socket joint of the hip
Pivot joint between the atlas and axis vertebrae
questions.e: The atlas (first neck vertebra) rotates around the axis (second neck vertebra) at a pivot joint, allowing side-to-side head movement. The knee is a hinge joint, which only allows back-and-forth movement, not rotation.
questions.p: Na pivot joint dey between atlas and axis vertebrae for neck, e dey make head turn sideways. Knee na hinge joint, e no fit rotate like dat, na only forward and backward e dey allow.

questions.q: A student examined a joint that allows movement in almost every direction - forward, backward, sideways and rotation. This kind of joint, called a ball and socket joint, is most likely found at the
questions.e: The shoulder joint is a ball and socket joint, formed by the rounded head of the humerus fitting into a cup-shaped socket of the shoulder blade. This structure allows the widest range of movement in the body, including rotation.
questions.p: Shoulder na ball and socket joint, wey be say the round head of the arm bone (humerus) dey fit enter the cup-like socket of shoulder bone. Na dis kind joint dey give the widest movement, including rotation.

questions.q: In a typical flower, which part develops into the fruit after successful fertilization has taken place?
questions.e: After fertilization, the ovary wall grows and develops into the fruit, while the ovules inside become the seeds. The stigma and anther do not form the fruit; they are involved in pollination only.
questions.p: After fertilization, na the ovary waka turn to fruit, while the ovules wey dey inside turn to seeds. Stigma and anther no dey form fruit, na only pollination work dem dey do.

questions.q: Mrs. Adebayo noticed that a bee carried pollen grains from the anther of a hibiscus flower in her garden to the stigma of another hibiscus flower growing on a different hibiscus plant nearby. This type of pollen transfer is called?
questions.e: Cross-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of a flower on one plant to the stigma of a flower on another plant of the same species. Self-pollination and autogamy happen within the same flower or same plant, while cleistogamy refers to pollination in flowers that never open.
questions.p: Cross-pollination na when pollen comot from anther of flower for one plant go land for stigma of flower for another plant wey be the same species. Self-pollination na when e happen inside the same flower or plant, while cleistogamy na pollination wey happen for flower wey never open at all.

questions.q: Which of the following floral features is an adaptation that helps a flower to be pollinated by wind?
o: Large feathery stigma that hangs outside the flower
Brightly coloured petals to attract insects
Sticky pollen grains produced in small quantities
questions.e: Wind-pollinated flowers have large, feathery stigmas that hang out of the flower to easily trap pollen grains floating in the air. They also produce light, dry pollen in large amounts, and usually lack bright colours, nectar or scent since they do not need to attract insects.
questions.p: Flower wey wind dey pollinate get big, feathery stigma wey dey hang comot from the flower so e fit catch pollen wey dey fly for air. Dem dey produce light, dry pollen for plenty quantity, and dem no need bright colour, nectar or sweet smell because na wind go carry dem, no be insect.

questions.q: A mango fruit has a soft fleshy outer covering, a juicy middle layer, and a single hard stony endocarp that encloses the seed. This type of fruit is correctly classified as a?
questions.e: A drupe is a fleshy fruit with a hard, stony endocarp enclosing a single seed, like mango and coconut. A berry has no hard endocarp (seeds are embedded directly in soft pulp), a pod is a dry dehiscent legume fruit, and a capsule is a dry fruit that splits open at maturity.
questions.p: Drupe na fleshy fruit wey get hard stony endocarp wey dey cover one seed, like mango and coconut. Berry no get hard endocarp (seeds dey inside soft pulp), pod na dry legume fruit wey dey open, capsule na dry fruit wey dey split open when e ripe.

questions.q: Some leguminous plants such as Bauhinia (camel's foot plant) produce pods that dry up, twist and suddenly burst open with force, scattering their seeds some distance away from the parent plant. This method of seed dispersal is best described as?
questions.e: When the pod dries and twists, tension builds up inside it until it bursts open suddenly, throwing the seeds some distance away without the help of wind, water or animals. This is called mechanical or explosive dispersal because the plant itself generates the force.
questions.p: As the pod dry and twist, force dey build up inside am until e burst open sharp sharp, e go throway the seeds far small without wind, water or animal helep. Na so dem dey call am mechanical or explosive dispersal because na the plant itself dey generate the force.

questions.q: Tunde wanted to germinate maize seeds for a school project. He soaked the seeds overnight, wrapped them in moist cotton wool, and sealed them tightly inside an airtight polythene bag which he kept at room temperature for one week. At the end of the week, the seeds had absorbed water and swollen but had still failed to germinate. Which condition necessary for germination was most likely lacking?
questions.e: Sealing the seeds in an airtight bag prevented fresh air from getting in, so the oxygen needed for aerobic respiration during germination quickly got used up. Water and temperature were clearly adequate since the seeds swelled at room temperature, and light is not required for germination.
questions.p: As Tunde seal the bag tight, fresh air no fit enter, so the oxygen wey the seeds need for respiration quick finish. Water and temperature no be problem at all because the seeds swell well for room temperature, and light no dey important for germination sef.

questions.q: In which of the following animals does fertilization normally take place outside the body of the female, in water?
questions.e: Tilapia and most fish release their eggs and sperm directly into water, where fertilization occurs outside the body. Goats, hens and dogs all have internal fertilization.
questions.p: Tilapia and most fish dey release their eggs and sperm for inside water, na there fertilization dey happen. Goat, hen and dog dey do internal fertilization inside their body.

questions.q: Which organ in the male mammalian reproductive system is mainly responsible for the production of spermatozoa?
questions.e: The testis contains seminiferous tubules where sperm cells are produced. The epididymis stores and matures sperm, the prostate gland adds seminal fluid, and the vas deferens only transports sperm.
questions.p: Na testis dey produce sperm cells inside the seminiferous tubules. Epididymis na where sperm dey mature and store, prostate gland dey add fluid, while vas deferens na just pipe wey sperm dey pass.

questions.q: An ovoviviparous animal can best be described as one that:
o: nourishes its developing young directly through a placenta before they are born
lays eggs that develop and hatch completely outside the mother's body
produces eggs that develop and hatch inside the mother's body, with the young getting little or no direct nourishment from her blood
reproduces only by budding, without forming eggs at all
questions.e: Ovoviviparous animals, like some sharks and certain snakes, keep their eggs inside the body until they hatch, but the young feed mainly from the yolk, not from the mother's blood directly. This is different from viviparous animals that use a placenta.
questions.p: Ovoviviparous animal, like some shark and snake, dey keep their eggs for inside body until e hatch, but the young ones dey chop from the yolk, no be mother blood directly. Na different thing from viviparous wey get placenta.

questions.q: A fowl's egg is cut open and a thick, clear, jelly-like substance surrounding the yolk is seen. This substance mainly serves to cushion and nourish the growing embryo. What is it called?
questions.e: The albumen, also called egg white, is the clear jelly-like substance that surrounds the yolk. It protects the embryo from shock and supplies extra protein and water for development.
questions.p: Na albumen, wey be the clear jelly-jelly substance around the yolk. E dey protect the embryo from shock and e dey give am protein and water make e grow well.

questions.q: In the human menstrual cycle, the sudden release of a mature egg from the ovary (ovulation) is mainly triggered by a sharp rise in which hormone?
questions.e: A sudden surge in Luteinizing Hormone (LH) around the middle of the cycle causes the mature follicle to rupture and release the egg. FSH mainly stimulates follicle growth earlier in the cycle, while progesterone and oestrogen act mostly after or before ovulation to prepare the uterus.
questions.p: Na sudden rise for Luteinizing Hormone (LH) for middle of the cycle dey make the follicle burst and release the egg. FSH dey help the follicle grow early for the cycle, while progesterone and oestrogen dey prepare the womb before or after ovulation.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines growth in living organisms?
o: A permanent and irreversible increase in size and dry weight of an organism
The production of new cells without any increase in overall size
An increase in body weight caused only by water absorption
A temporary increase in size that can later be reversed
questions.e: Growth is a permanent, irreversible increase in size, mass and dry weight due to addition of new cells and materials. Water uptake alone (swelling) is temporary and not true growth.
questions.p: Growth na permanent increase wey no fit come back for size, body weight and dry weight of living thing. If na only water enter body make e swell, e no be real growth because e fit go back.

questions.q: Which plant hormone is mainly responsible for cell elongation in the shoot tip and causes a growing shoot to bend towards a source of light?
questions.e: Auxin is produced at the shoot tip and promotes cell elongation. Its unequal distribution towards the shaded side makes that side grow faster, bending the shoot towards light (phototropism).
questions.p: Auxin dey produce for shoot tip, e dey make cell dey long well well. E dey pack more for the shaded side, so dat side go grow pass, make the shoot bend go where light dey.

questions.q: A farmer notices that some maize seedlings in his farm in Kaduna are unusually short compared to others. If he wants to make these dwarf seedlings grow as tall as the normal ones, which hormone would most likely help by promoting stem elongation?
questions.e: Gibberellins are well known for promoting stem elongation, and applying them to genetically dwarf plants can make them grow tall like normal varieties. This is a classic effect used in agriculture.
questions.p: Gibberellin na the hormone wey sabi make stem grow long. If dem apply am for short (dwarf) plant, e fit make the plant grow tall like the normal ones.

questions.q: A young boy shows signs of stunted growth and slow mental development because his thyroid gland is not producing enough hormone. Which hormone is deficient in this boy?
questions.e: Thyroxine, secreted by the thyroid gland, controls metabolic rate and is essential for normal physical and mental growth in children. Its deficiency in childhood causes cretinism, marked by stunted growth and poor mental development.
questions.p: Thyroxine na the hormone wey the thyroid gland dey produce, e dey control how body dey use energy and e important for growth and brain. If pikin no get am well, e fit cause short body and slow brain, dem dey call am cretinism.

questions.q: A potted seedling was kept in a closed box with a small opening that allowed light to enter from only one side. After several days, the shoot was observed to bend towards the opening. This bending happens because auxin produced at the shoot tip...
o: accumulates more on the illuminated side, making it grow faster than the shaded side
accumulates more on the shaded side, making it elongate faster than the illuminated side, so the shoot curves towards the light
is produced only on the illuminated side and has no effect on the shaded side
remains equally distributed on both sides, so bending is not caused by auxin at all
questions.e: Auxin moves away from the light to the shaded side of the shoot. The shaded side therefore has more auxin and its cells elongate faster than those on the lit side, pushing the tip to curve towards the light. This unequal growth, not light itself, causes the bending.
questions.p: Auxin dey waka comot from where light dey go the shaded side of the shoot. So the shaded side get more auxin, the cells for there grow pass the one wey light dey shine on. Na im make the shoot bend go where light dey.

questions.q: In the typical S-shaped (sigmoid) growth curve of a population of organisms, which phase shows the population size increasing most rapidly, that is, the fastest rate of growth?
questions.e: In the log (exponential) phase, organisms have plenty of food and space, so they reproduce rapidly and population size increases at its fastest rate. The lag phase is slow adjustment, while the stationary and decline phases show levelling off or reduction.
questions.p: For log (exponential) phase, food and space still dey plenty, so the organisms dey multiply quick quick, na there population dey increase pass. Lag phase na slow start, while stationary and decline phase na where e stop to increase or e begin reduce.

questions.q: In a neuron, which part receives nerve impulses from neighbouring neurons and passes them towards the cell body?
questions.e: Dendrites are branch-like extensions that receive impulses from other neurons and carry them towards the cell body. The axon carries impulses away from the cell body instead.
questions.p: Dendrite na di one wey dey receive message from oda neurons go di cell body. Axon na di one wey dey carry di message comot from cell body.

questions.q: Which of these human actions is a reflex action?
o: Withdrawing the hand quickly after touching a hot pot
questions.e: A reflex action is a quick, automatic response to a stimulus that does not require conscious thought. Withdrawing the hand from a hot pot happens instantly without thinking, unlike writing, walking or solving maths which are voluntary actions.
questions.p: Reflex action na quick response wey body dey do automatic, no need to think. To quick remove hand from hot pot na reflex, but to waka or write exam na thing wey person dey think before e do am.

questions.q: A student is asked to arrange the events of a simple reflex arc in the correct order, starting from when a stimulus is detected to when a response is produced. The events are: (1) effector produces a response, (2) receptor detects the stimulus, (3) relay neuron in the spinal cord processes the impulse, (4) sensory neuron carries the impulse to the spinal cord, (5) motor neuron carries the impulse to the effector. What is the correct order?
questions.e: In a reflex arc, the receptor first detects the stimulus, the sensory neuron carries the impulse to the spinal cord, the relay neuron processes it, the motor neuron carries it to the effector, and the effector finally produces the response. This gives the order 2, 4, 3, 5, 1.
questions.p: Di correct order na: receptor go first detect di stimulus, den sensory neuron go carry di message go spinal cord, relay neuron go process am, motor neuron go carry am go effector, den effector go bring out di response. So na 2,4,3,5,1.

questions.q: The small gap between two adjacent neurons, across which a nerve impulse is transmitted by means of chemical substances, is called the
questions.e: The synapse is the junction between two neurons where chemical substances called neurotransmitters cross the gap to pass the impulse from one neuron to the next. The node of Ranvier and myelin sheath are found along the axon, not between two neurons.
questions.p: Synapse na di small gap between two neurons where chemical substance (neurotransmitter) dey carry message from one neuron go anoda one. Node of Ranvier and myelin sheath dey inside di axon, no be between two neurons.

questions.q: Which part of the human brain is mainly responsible for maintaining balance and coordinating muscular movements, such as when riding a bicycle?
questions.e: The cerebellum controls balance, posture and coordination of voluntary muscular movements. The cerebrum deals with thinking and memory, the hypothalamus regulates body temperature and hunger, while the medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions like heartbeat and breathing.
questions.p: Cerebellum na di part wey dey control balance and how muscle dey coordinate well-well, like for bicycle riding. Cerebrum dey handle thinking, hypothalamus dey control temperature and hunger, medulla oblongata dey control heartbeat and breathing.

questions.q: During a knee-jerk reflex test, a doctor taps the tendon just below a patient's kneecap and the patient's lower leg kicks forward almost immediately, without the patient thinking about it. Which feature of the reflex arc best explains why the response happens so quickly?
o: The impulse is carried slowly by hormones through the bloodstream
The impulse passes through many relay neurons in the cerebrum before reaching the muscle
The sensory neuron contracts the muscle directly without passing through any synapse
The impulse bypasses the brain and travels through only a few neurons in the spinal cord
questions.e: In a simple reflex like the knee-jerk, the impulse travels a short path through the spinal cord only, involving very few neurons and synapses, and does not go to the brain for conscious processing. This short pathway makes the response very fast compared to actions controlled by the brain.
questions.p: Dis knee-jerk reflex dey fast because di message no reach brain at all, e just dey pass small-small neurons for inside spinal cord. Since di road wey di message take dey short, di response go sharp pass action wey brain go first process.

questions.q: Which part of the human eye controls the amount of light that enters the eye?
questions.e: The iris is the coloured, muscular part of the eye that widens or narrows the pupil to control how much light enters. The retina receives the image, the cornea refracts light, and the lens focuses it, but none of these controls light quantity.
questions.p: Na iris dey control how much light dey enter eye, e be like the colourful part wey dey open or close the pupil. Retina na where image dey land, cornea and lens dey bend light make e focus well, but na only iris dey control light amount.

questions.q: Which structure in the human ear is mainly responsible for maintaining body balance?
questions.e: The semicircular canals contain fluid that moves when the head changes position, sending balance signals to the brain. The cochlea deals with hearing, the eardrum vibrates with sound, and the auditory nerve only carries sound signals.
questions.p: Na semicircular canals get the liquid wey dey move anytime head change position, e dey send balance message go brain. Cochlea na for hearing, eardrum na im dey vibrate with sound, auditory nerve na only sound message e dey carry.

questions.q: Which layer of the human skin contains sweat glands, hair follicles and blood vessels?
questions.e: The dermis is the thicker inner layer of the skin that houses sweat glands, hair follicles, blood vessels and nerve endings. The epidermis is the outer protective layer without these structures, while the subcutaneous layer mainly stores fat.
questions.p: Na dermis, the inner layer wey thick, get sweat glands, hair follicles, blood vessels and nerves. Epidermis na the outer layer wey dey protect body, e no get all these things, while the fat layer wey dey under dey store fat.

questions.q: Ngozi walks straight from a dark cinema hall into bright afternoon sunlight. What immediate change occurs in her eyes?
o: The cornea thickens to block excess light
The pupil dilates to allow more light in
The lens becomes more convex to focus near objects
The pupil constricts to reduce the amount of light entering
questions.e: In bright light, the circular muscles of the iris contract, making the pupil smaller (constrict) to reduce the amount of light entering and protect the retina. Dilation happens in dim light, not bright light, and the cornea does not thicken to control light.
questions.p: When light bright reach, the round muscle for iris go tighten make pupil small (constrict) so e go reduce the light wey dey enter, to protect retina. Na for dark place pupil dey dilate (open big), cornea no dey thicken to block light.

questions.q: During a cultural dance in his village, Chidi spins round quickly many times and immediately feels dizzy and unsteady when he stops. Which structure is mainly responsible for this feeling of imbalance?
o: Semicircular canals, because the fluid inside keeps moving briefly after he stops spinning
Eustachian tube, because it equalizes air pressure in the middle ear
Cochlea, because it is responsible for hearing
Pinna, because it collects and directs sound waves
questions.e: The semicircular canals contain fluid (endolymph) that moves as the head turns; when Chidi suddenly stops, the fluid keeps moving for a short time, sending false balance signals to the brain, causing dizziness. The cochlea, pinna and Eustachian tube are involved in hearing or pressure, not balance.
questions.p: Semicircular canals get liquid (endolymph) wey dey move as head dey turn; when Chidi stop sharp-sharp, the liquid still dey move small small, e go send wrong balance message go brain make e feel dizzy. Cochlea, pinna and Eustachian tube na for hearing and pressure, no be balance.

questions.q: On a very hot afternoon in Lagos, Bisi notices her skin looking flushed as the blood vessels near the skin surface widen (vasodilation). What is the main effect of this vasodilation?
o: It reduces blood flow to the skin to conserve body heat
It makes the hair erector muscles contract to trap warm air
It increases heat loss from the body through radiation at the skin surface
It stops the sweat glands from releasing sweat
questions.e: When blood vessels near the skin surface widen (vasodilate), more warm blood flows close to the surface, allowing more body heat to escape by radiation, which helps cool the body. This is the opposite of conserving heat, and it does not involve hair erector muscles or stopping sweating, which would actually increase to cool the body further.
questions.p: When blood vessels near skin surface open wide (vasodilate), plenty warm blood dey flow near the surface, e go make heat waste comot from body through radiation, so body go cool down. E no be heat-conserving action, and e no concern hair muscle or stopping sweat — sweating go even increase to help cool body.

questions.q: Which term describes a community of living organisms interacting with each other and with their non-living (physical) environment, functioning together as a unit?
questions.e: An ecosystem is made up of living organisms (biotic factors) and the non-living environment (abiotic factors) interacting together. A habitat is just where an organism lives, while a population is a group of the same species. The biosphere is the whole part of the Earth that supports life.
questions.p: Ecosystem na when living tins and the environment dem dey work together as one unit. Habitat na just where animal dey stay, population na only one kind animal, biosphere na the whole world wey get life.

questions.q: In a farmland food chain in a village near Enugu: maize plant -> grasshopper -> lizard -> hawk, which organism is the primary consumer?
questions.e: The maize plant is the producer because it makes its own food. The grasshopper feeds directly on the maize, so it is the primary consumer. The lizard that eats the grasshopper is the secondary consumer, and the hawk is the tertiary consumer.
questions.p: Maize na producer because e dey make im own food. Grasshopper na the one wey dey chop the maize direct, so na im be primary consumer. Lizard na secondary consumer, hawk na tertiary consumer.

questions.q: During energy flow in an ecosystem, only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is passed on to the next level, the rest is lost as heat and through respiration. If producers in a Niger Delta swamp forest contain 20,000 kJ of energy, how much energy would be available to the secondary consumers?
questions.e: Producers (20,000 kJ) pass 10% to primary consumers: 20,000 x 10/100 = 2,000 kJ. Primary consumers then pass 10% to secondary consumers: 2,000 x 10/100 = 200 kJ. So secondary consumers get 200 kJ.
questions.p: Producer get 20,000 kJ, 10% of am go reach primary consumer: 20,000 x 10/100 = 2,000 kJ. Then 10% of the 2,000 kJ go reach secondary consumer: 2,000 x 10/100 = 200 kJ.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes how energy flows through an ecosystem?
o: Energy flow is equal at every trophic level without any loss
Energy flows in one direction, from producers to consumers, with some energy lost as heat at each stage
Energy is reused repeatedly by organisms at different trophic levels
Energy flows from consumers back to producers in a complete cycle
questions.e: Unlike nutrients, energy does not cycle back; it flows one way from the sun to producers and then to the various consumers, with energy lost as heat at each transfer (mostly through respiration). This is why energy flow is described as unidirectional, unlike the cycling of materials such as carbon or nitrogen.
questions.p: Energy no dey cycle back like nutrients, e dey flow one way from sun go producer go consumer, and some dey waste as heat for each level. Na why dem dey call am one-way flow, e no be like carbon or nitrogen wey dey cycle.

questions.q: A Biology teacher asked her SS3 class why food chains in nature rarely have more than four or five trophic levels. Which of these is the best scientific reason?
o: Predators at higher trophic levels refuse to reproduce after some generations
Decomposers destroy all organisms before they can be eaten by predators
Producers are not able to make enough biomass to support more than five levels
Energy is lost as heat at each trophic level, so there is not enough energy left to support more levels
questions.e: At each trophic level, a large amount of energy is lost as heat during respiration and other life processes, so only about 10% is passed to the next level. After 4-5 transfers, the remaining energy becomes too small to support another feeding level, which is why food chains are usually short.
questions.p: For every level, plenty energy dey waste as heat during respiration, so na small percent (like 10%) dey pass go the next level. After 4 to 5 levels, the energy wey remain too small to carry another level, na why food chain no dey too long.

questions.q: A student studying a fish pond near Badagry recorded the following energy content at different trophic levels: phytoplankton = 8,000 kJ, zooplankton = 800 kJ, small fish = 80 kJ. What percentage of the energy in the zooplankton was transferred to the small fish?
questions.e: Percentage transferred = (energy in small fish / energy in zooplankton) x 100 = (80/800) x 100 = 10%. This shows the typical 10% rule of energy transfer between trophic levels in an ecosystem.
questions.p: Percentage wey transfer = (80/800) x 100 = 10%. Na the normal 10% rule wey dey happen anytime energy dey pass from one trophic level go another.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a 'population' in ecological studies?
o: The physical place where a particular organism normally lives
All the different species of organisms living together in a habitat at the same time
All the living and non-living components found in an environment
All the individuals of the same species living in a particular area at the same time
questions.e: A population refers only to members of one species found together in a given area at a given time. This is different from a community (many species together) or an ecosystem (living plus non-living things).
questions.p: Population na all the members of one kind of animal or plant wey dey live for one place one time. E no be community (wey get many different species) or ecosystem (wey get living and non-living things togeda).

questions.q: In ecology, which term describes the specific role, function and position that an organism occupies in its habitat, including how it obtains food and relates with other organisms?
questions.e: The niche of an organism is its functional role and relationship with other living things and the environment, not just the place where it lives (which is the habitat).
questions.p: Niche na the role and work wey organism get for im environment, e include how e dey find chop and relate wit oda living things. Habitat na just where e dey stay, e no be di same as niche.

questions.q: A certain large mammal found in arid regions has nostrils that can close completely, very long eyelashes, thick padded feet, and kidneys that produce highly concentrated urine. These features are adaptations for survival in which type of habitat?
questions.e: Closable nostrils and long eyelashes keep out blowing sand, padded feet prevent sinking in loose sand, and concentrated urine conserves water — all are classic adaptations of animals like the camel that live in hot, dry desert conditions.
questions.p: Nose wey fit close well-well, long eyelash, padded leg and strong concentrated urine na adaptation for camel wey dey live for desert. Dis features dey help am manage sand and save water for hot dry place.

questions.q: A certain floating plant has broad flat leaves, stomata located mainly on the upper surface of the leaf, and large air spaces (aerenchyma) inside its leaf and stem tissues. This combination of features best suits the plant to which type of habitat?
questions.e: Plants like the water lily float on water; stomata on the upper leaf surface allow gas exchange since the lower surface touches water, and air spaces give buoyancy and help carry oxygen to submerged parts — typical hydrophyte adaptations.
questions.p: Dis kind plant like water lily dey float for water, stomata dey for di top side because di down side dey touch water, and air space inside di leaf dey help am float and carry oxygen go di part wey dey inside water. Na water plant adaptation be dis.

questions.q: A student wanted to estimate the population of grasshoppers in a school football field using the capture-recapture method. She first caught 40 grasshoppers, marked them with a harmless dye, and released them back into the field. Three days later, she caught 50 grasshoppers from the same field, out of which 20 were found to carry the mark. Using the Lincoln index, estimate the total population of grasshoppers in the field.
questions.e: Lincoln index: Population (N) = (number first caught and marked x number caught second time) / number marked found in second catch = (40 x 50) / 20 = 100.
questions.p: Lincoln index formula: N = (number wey dem first catch and mark x number wey dem catch second time) ÷ number wey get mark for di second catch = (40 x 50) ÷ 20 = 100.

questions.q: A cassava farm in Benue State measures 500 square metres and contains exactly 250 cassava plants evenly spread across the farm. Calculate the population density of the cassava plants in plants per square metre.
questions.e: Population density = number of organisms / area occupied = 250 / 500 = 0.5 plants per square metre.
questions.p: Population density = number of plant ÷ di area wey dem dey = 250 ÷ 500 = 0.5 plant for every square metre.

questions.q: Which of the following processes directly returns carbon(IV) oxide to the atmosphere during the carbon cycle?
o: Formation of limestone in the sea
Absorption of carbon by the soil
questions.e: Respiration breaks down food and releases carbon(IV) oxide as a waste product into the air. Photosynthesis does the opposite by removing carbon(IV) oxide from the air. Limestone formation and soil absorption do not release the gas back to the atmosphere.
questions.p: Respiration na im dey bring carbon(IV) oxide comot back to air as waste. Photosynthesis na im dey remove the gas from air, so na opposite. Limestone and soil no dey release the gas like that.

questions.q: The process by which atmospheric nitrogen gas is converted into a form that plants can use is called:
questions.e: Nitrogen fixation is the process that changes free nitrogen gas in the air into nitrogen compounds like ammonia or nitrates that plants can absorb. Ammonification produces ammonia from dead organisms, while denitrification releases nitrogen gas back to air. Nitrification converts ammonia to nitrates, not atmospheric nitrogen directly.
questions.p: Nitrogen fixation na the process wey dey change the nitrogen gas for air to form wey plant fit use. Ammonification na from dead things dem dey make ammonia, denitrification dey release nitrogen gas back to air. Nitrification na to change ammonia to nitrate, e no be from air nitrogen.

questions.q: In a school farm at Nkwerre, Mrs. Okafor observed root nodules on cowpea plants. These nodules contain bacteria that help the plant by:
o: Absorbing excess water from the soil
Converting nitrates back to nitrogen gas
Breaking down dead leaves into humus
Fixing atmospheric nitrogen into usable nitrogen compounds
questions.e: Leguminous plants like cowpea have root nodules containing Rhizobium bacteria that fix nitrogen gas from the air into nitrogen compounds the plant can use. This is why legumes can grow well even in poor soils. The other options describe different processes not linked to root nodules.
questions.p: Cowpea na legume, and the bacteria for im root nodule dey take nitrogen gas from air change am to form wey plant go fit use. Na why legume dey grow well even for bad soil. The other options no relate to wetin dey happen for root nodule.

questions.q: Which stage of the water cycle involves the loss of water vapour from the leaves of plants?
questions.e: Transpiration is specifically the loss of water vapour from plant leaves through tiny pores called stomata. Evaporation refers to water loss from open surfaces like rivers and oceans, not plant leaves. Condensation and precipitation are stages that occur in the atmosphere, not at the leaf surface.
questions.p: Transpiration na when water vapour dey comot from plant leaf through stomata. Evaporation na water wey dey comot from river or ocean surface, no be from leaf. Condensation and precipitation dey happen for sky, no be for leaf.

questions.q: A farmer notices that his waterlogged rice field has a bad smell and his crop yield reduces despite applying nitrate fertilizer. This is most likely because:
o: Nitrifying bacteria convert ammonia to nitrates faster in waterlogged soil
Water dissolves all the nitrate and washes it permanently out of the field
Denitrifying bacteria thrive in the oxygen-poor soil and release nitrogen gas into the air
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in root nodules stop working in wet soil
questions.e: Waterlogged soil has little oxygen, which favours denitrifying bacteria that convert nitrates back into nitrogen gas, reducing the nitrogen available to the rice plants. This explains both the yield loss and the smell from anaerobic bacterial activity. The other options do not correctly explain the oxygen-poor condition's effect on nitrogen loss.
questions.p: When soil waterlogged, oxygen dey reduce, and dat kind condition good for denitrifying bacteria wey dey change nitrate back to nitrogen gas, so e dey reduce nitrogen wey rice go use. Na why yield go reduce and bad smell go dey from the bacteria work. The other options no explain the low oxygen effect well.

questions.q: In a stable ecosystem, the amount of carbon(IV) oxide released into the atmosphere by respiration is roughly balanced by the amount removed through photosynthesis. If deforestation drastically reduces the number of trees in an area, what is the most likely long-term effect on the carbon cycle in that area?
o: The rate of respiration by animals will reduce to compensate
Carbon(IV) oxide levels in the atmosphere will decrease steadily
Carbon(IV) oxide levels in the atmosphere will increase over time
Oxygen levels will rise sharply above normal levels
questions.e: Trees remove carbon(IV) oxide from the air through photosynthesis, so fewer trees mean less carbon(IV) oxide is absorbed while respiration continues to release it. This imbalance causes carbon(IV) oxide to build up in the atmosphere over time. Animal respiration rates do not naturally reduce to fix this imbalance.
questions.p: Trees dey use photosynthesis take absorb carbon(IV) oxide, so if trees reduce, less gas go dey absorb but respiration still dey release am. This mean say carbon(IV) oxide go dey accumulate for air with time. Animal respiration no go just reduce to balance am.

questions.q: Which of the following insects is the vector responsible for transmitting the parasite that causes malaria in humans?
questions.e: The female Anopheles mosquito carries the Plasmodium parasite and passes it into the blood of a person when it bites to feed. Male mosquitoes do not bite humans because they feed on plant nectar, not blood.
questions.p: Na female Anopheles mosquito dey carry the Plasmodium parasite wey dey cause malaria, e dey enter person body when e bite. Male mosquito no dey bite human because e dey feed on nectar from plant.

questions.q: A pest can be best defined as any organism that
o: lives permanently inside another organism without harming it
competes with man for food, destroys his crops or transmits disease
helps in pollination of flowering plants
decomposes dead organic matter in the soil
questions.e: A pest is any organism that is harmful to man, either by destroying his crops, stored food, animals or by spreading disease. Decomposers and pollinators are usually beneficial, not harmful.
questions.p: Pest na any living thing wey dey cause wahala for man, like e go spoil im crop, food, animal or spread sickness. Decomposer and pollinator dey help man, dem no be pest.

questions.q: Which of these diseases is mainly spread through contaminated water and poor sanitation?
questions.e: Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae bacteria that spread through water or food contaminated with faecal matter, especially where sanitation is poor. Measles and tuberculosis spread through air droplets, while tetanus enters through wounds.
questions.p: Cholera na sickness wey Vibrio cholerae bacteria dey cause, e dey spread through water or food wey shit don enter, especially where sanitation no good. Measles and TB dey spread through air, tetanus dey enter through wound.

questions.q: A school health club in Enugu wants to reduce the breeding of mosquitoes around the hostel compound. Which of the following practices would be most effective?
o: Planting more flowering shrubs near the hostel
Increasing the number of dustbins around the compound
Clearing stagnant water in drains and covering water storage containers
Spraying the classrooms with insecticide once a term
