questions.e: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in stagnant water, so removing or covering such water stops the larvae from developing into adults. Spraying classrooms only kills adult mosquitoes temporarily and does not stop new ones from breeding.
questions.p: Mosquito dey lay egg for still water, so if you clear am or cover am well, the larvae no go fit grow to adult mosquito. To spray classroom just dey kill the adult ones small time, e no dey stop new ones from breeding.

questions.q: Mr. Okafor's farm recorded heavy loss of yam tubers due to rot caused by nematodes in the soil. Which farming practice would best help reduce this pest's population before the next planting season?
o: Reducing the spacing between yam plants
Continuous planting of yam on the same plot every season
Applying excess nitrogen fertilizer to the soil
Crop rotation with a non-host crop such as maize
questions.e: Crop rotation with a crop that nematodes cannot feed on, such as maize, breaks their life cycle because they lose their host and their population reduces over time. Planting yam continuously keeps feeding the nematodes and allows them to multiply.
questions.p: If Mr. Okafor rotate im farm make e plant maize wey nematode no fit chop, the nematode no go get food again and e go reduce small small. But if e dey plant yam every season for the same land, e dey give the nematode food to continue to multiply.

questions.q: A community recorded an outbreak of a disease that caused yellowing of the eyes, dark urine and fatigue among residents who often ate shellfish from a polluted river. Which disease is most likely responsible?
questions.e: Hepatitis A is a liver infection caused by a virus found in water or food, such as shellfish, contaminated by faecal matter, and it causes jaundice (yellow eyes), dark urine and tiredness because the liver is affected. Guinea worm, onchocerciasis and schistosomiasis do not cause jaundice as their main symptom.
questions.p: Hepatitis A na liver sickness wey virus dey cause, e dey enter body through water or food like shellfish wey don mix with shit, and e dey make eye yellow, urine dark and body weak because liver don spoil. Guinea worm, onchocerciasis and schistosomiasis no dey cause jaundice like dat.

questions.q: In genetics, the actual genetic make-up of an organism, which controls its characteristics but may not always be seen outwardly, is called the
questions.e: Genotype is the set of genes an organism carries for a trait, while phenotype is the physical expression of those genes. Genotype can be hidden if the gene is recessive.
questions.p: Genotype na di gene wey dey inside body wey dey control character, e fit no show for outside. Phenotype na wetin we see for outside.

questions.q: Which of the following human traits is an example of discontinuous variation?
questions.e: Blood group falls into distinct classes (A, B, AB, O) with no in-between forms, so it is discontinuous. Height, weight and skin colour show a range of values, making them continuous.
questions.p: Blood group get clear categories like A, B, AB, O, no mixture dey between dem, so na discontinuous. Height, weight and skin colour dey change small small, so na continuous.

questions.q: In maize, tallness (T) is dominant over shortness (t). A heterozygous tall maize plant (Tt) is crossed with a short plant (tt). What is the expected ratio of tall to short offspring?
questions.e: Tt x tt gives gametes T,t from one parent and t,t from the other, producing Tt and tt offspring in equal numbers. This gives a 1:1 ratio of tall to short plants.
questions.p: Tt x tt go give Tt and tt offspring for equal number. So di ratio of tall to short na 1:1.

questions.q: A man with normal colour vision marries a woman who is a carrier for colour blindness (heterozygous, X^N X^n). What proportion of their sons is expected to be colour blind?
questions.e: Sons get their X chromosome from the mother only. Since she is X^N X^n, half her eggs carry X^n, so half of the sons (X^n Y) will be colour blind.
questions.p: Boy pikin dey collect im X chromosome from mama only. Since mama na X^N X^n, half of her eggs get X^n, so half of di boys go be colour blind.

questions.q: In guinea pigs, black coat (B) is dominant over white (b), and short hair (H) is dominant over long hair (h). A guinea pig heterozygous for both traits (BbHh) is crossed with a white, long-haired guinea pig (bbhh). What fraction of the offspring is expected to be black and short-haired?
questions.e: This is a test cross (BbHh x bbhh), which gives four phenotypes in equal 1:1:1:1 ratio. So black, short-haired offspring make up 1/4 of the total.
questions.p: Na test cross be dis (BbHh x bbhh), e go give four phenotypes for equal 1:1:1:1 ratio. So black, short hair go be 1/4 of di total pikin dem.

questions.q: A man with blood group AB marries a woman with blood group O. Considering that blood group O is genotype ii while AB has both I^A and I^B alleles, what blood groups can their children have?
questions.e: The AB parent gives either I^A or I^B gametes, while the O parent gives only i gametes. Combining these gives genotypes I^A i (blood group A) or I^B i (blood group B), so the children can only be group A or B.
questions.p: Papa wey be AB go give I^A or I^B, mama wey be O go give only i. If you combine dem, you go get I^A i (A) or I^B i (B), so di pikin dem fit be only A or B.

questions.q: In biology, which of the following best describes 'evolution'?
o: Seasonal change in the colour of an organism's skin
Sudden change in an organism within one generation due to injury
Change in the diet of an organism as it grows older
Gradual change in the inherited characteristics of organisms over many generations, which can lead to new species
questions.e: Evolution is the slow, continuous change in the inherited traits of a population over long periods, which can eventually lead to new species. It is not a change that happens within a single organism's lifetime.
questions.p: Evolution na as living things dey change small-small for inherited traits over plenty generations, until e fit bring new kind species. E no be sudden change wey one animal go experience for im own lifetime.

questions.q: According to Charles Darwin's theory of natural selection, which statement best explains why certain organisms survive and reproduce more successfully than others in a given environment?
o: All organisms in a population have equal chances of survival regardless of their traits
Organisms with inherited traits best suited to their environment survive and pass on these traits to their offspring
Organisms acquire new traits during their lifetime and pass these directly to their offspring
Organisms that reproduce the most always have the weakest traits
questions.e: Natural selection states that organisms with favourable inherited traits are better suited to survive and reproduce in their environment, passing these traits to the next generation. This is often summarised as 'survival of the fittest.'
questions.p: Darwin talk say na organisms wey get better inherited traits for their environment go survive well well and born pikin wey go carry dat trait. Dis one na im dem dey call 'survival of the fittest.'

questions.q: A Lamarckian (pre-Darwin) explanation for the long neck of the modern giraffe would state that:
o: Giraffes stretched their necks to reach high leaves during their lifetime, and this acquired longer neck was passed directly to their offspring
Random mutation produced long necks, which were then favoured by the environment
Giraffes migrated to areas with taller trees, so their offspring were instantly born with longer necks
Giraffes with naturally longer necks were better suited to escape predators and survived
questions.e: Lamarck's theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics proposed that body changes gained during an organism's life, such as neck-stretching, could be passed on to offspring. Modern genetics has disproved this idea, unlike Darwin's natural selection.
questions.p: Lamarck theory talk say giraffe dey stretch dia neck throughout dia life to reach high leaves, and dat stretched neck dem go pass give their pikin direct. Science don show say dis idea no correct, unlike Darwin own.

questions.q: Mr. Adeyemi, a biology teacher, showed his students the bone structure of a man's arm, a bat's wing, and a whale's flipper. Although these limbs look different and perform different functions, they all share the same basic arrangement of bones (humerus, radius, ulna, and digits). This similarity is best explained as evidence of:
o: Analogous structures that evolved separately for the same function in unrelated species
Artificial selection carried out deliberately by early humans on these animals
Common ancestry, where these organisms evolved from a shared ancestor and later adapted the same basic limb structure for different functions
Convergent evolution, where unrelated organisms independently evolve similar structures for the same function
questions.e: Structures with the same basic plan but different functions in different species are called homologous structures. They provide strong evidence of common ancestry, since the basic design was inherited from a shared ancestor and later modified for different uses.
questions.p: When different animals get the same bone arrangement but the limb dey do different work, we dey call am homologous structures. Dis one na strong evidence say dem get common ancestor wey dem inherit the basic design from, before e later change for different work.

questions.q: Before industrialisation, the peppered moth population in parts of England was mostly light-coloured, blending well with lichen-covered tree trunks. After industrial pollution darkened the tree trunks with soot, the dark-coloured form of the moth became more common. What is the best explanation for this change?
o: Dark moths were better camouflaged against the sooty trunks, so they were less likely to be eaten by predators, survived and reproduced more, passing the dark trait to their offspring
Pollution directly changed the moths' genes, turning light moths into dark moths within one generation
Dark moths migrated into the area from other countries and completely replaced the light moths
Light moths deliberately changed their colour to match the new environment to avoid predators
questions.e: This is a classic case of natural selection known as industrial melanism. Dark moths were camouflaged against soot-darkened tree trunks, so predators found them harder to spot, meaning more dark moths survived and reproduced, increasing their numbers in the population.
questions.p: Dis na clear example of natural selection wey dem dey call industrial melanism. Dark moths blend well with the dirty black trees, so bird no too see dem to chop. Na why dark moths survive more and born plenty pikin, so dia number increase well well.

questions.q: In humans, the appendix is a small, finger-like structure attached to the large intestine. It has little or no digestive function in modern humans but is believed to have helped digest plant material in human ancestors. Structures like the appendix, which have lost most of their original function through evolution, are called:
questions.e: Vestigial structures are body parts that have become reduced and lost most or all of their original function during evolution, but are still present because they were useful in ancestral species. The appendix is a classic human example.
questions.p: Vestigial structures na body parts wey don reduce and lose their original work small-small as evolution dey happen, but dem still dey there because dem useful for our ancestors. Appendix na correct example for human being.
